releaseNote.summary: Pooled HTTP task clients with operator pool dials on both hosts; sub-item terminal lock waits start at 20 ms and stop as soon as the other delivery has settled the work.

httpTaskClientPool.description: The named HTTP clients every http/soap task (and the deprecated type-22 External HTTP task) sends through are now built on a pooled SocketsHttpHandler by one shared factory (WorkflowHttpMessageHandlerFactory) on both hosts, registered with an infinite handler lifetime. Before, IHttpClientFactory rotated an HttpClientHandler every two minutes, which discarded every warm TCP+TLS connection to the gateway at low traffic and made the next task pay the handshake again (measured 244 ms first call vs 76 ms warm to one APISIX host). Connection retirement is now per connection: Workflow:TaskInvocation:PooledConnectionLifetimeSeconds (default 600, bounds how long a DNS or gateway change can go unnoticed) and Workflow:TaskInvocation:PooledConnectionIdleTimeoutSeconds (default 120, keep it below the gateway's keep-alive timeout) join the existing Workflow:TaskInvocation:MaxConnectionsPerServer (default 50) on Orchestration. The Execution host's equivalent clients, whose cap was a hardcoded 10, read the same three dials from a new WorkflowHttpClient section (WorkflowHttpClientOptions) with the same defaults, so a task sees one connection policy whichever host performs the call; an environment that overrides one host's cap should override the other to match before reverting a hot single-target type to Remote.

subItemTerminalLockWaitReprobe.description: The SubFlow completion, fault and cancellation services take a bounded wait on the per-sub-item terminal lock because every terminal signal is delivered twice by design (post-commit relay plus Inbox backup). That wait's backoff is linear in its base delay, and the base was 120 ms (4 attempts): the backup that landed while the relay still held the lock slept 120-240 ms before its first retry, for a critical section of a few tens of milliseconds, and then found the correlation already closed (digital-investment, 2026-11-02: 2 of 11 sequential starts, 154 and 169 ms each). WorkflowExecutionOptions:SubItemTerminalLockRetry now defaults to 10 attempts x 20 ms (same ~1 s budget, 20-40 ms first retry), and the wait re-probes the correlation after every sleep through LockAcquireWait.KeepWaiting (wired by SubItemTerminalGuardExtensions.WhileCorrelationOpen): once the lock-free probe answers settled the wait is abandoned (Lock.Acquire span tag vnext.lock.wait_abandoned=true, subflow result correlation_already_settled_during_wait) instead of acquiring the lock only to load the parent and discover the work done. A not-acquired answer is re-probed once more before it becomes a SubflowTerminalLockNotAcquiredException, so an abandoned wait never turns into a broker redelivery. The state channel's own backoff (SubItemStateLockRetry, 10 x 10 ms) is unchanged.
